name: Kara Jackson
label: September Recordings
lede: Kara Jackson was a slam poet from Oak Park when she was named U.S. National Youth Poet Laureate. Four years later came a folk debut that asks the question most folk records dodge.

eras.title: Poems before songs
eras.text: Jackson grew up in Oak Park, Illinois, and came up through Chicago's youth poetry scene before she released a song. Her first audience was a slam stage, and her first bandmate-to-be was a best friend who didn't live to start the band.

years.src: The Line of Best Fit: Kara Jackson, love is as love does · Smith College: Music To Love
years.h: Maya-Gabrielle Gary, her best friend, dies of a rare muscle cancer
years.p: The two had bonded over the Beatles and a classic rock Tumblr, and planned a band together. Gary had played down her illness when she first told Jackson about it.
years.xp:
Jackson told The Line of Best Fit she didn't grasp how serious it was. Her favourite Beatle was George; Gary's was John. The first song Gary ever performed was "Put Your Records On" by Corinne Bailey Rae.

The debut album is dedicated to Gary's memory. Smith College later described it as honoring a high school friend lost to cancer.

years.src: Wikipedia: Kara Jackson · The Line of Best Fit: Kara Jackson, love is as love does
years.h: Chicago names her its Youth Poet Laureate
years.p: Jackson, then at Oak Park River Forest High School, performed at the Louder Than a Bomb finals and won the Literary Award, chosen by poet Patricia Smith.
years.xp: Smith praised her chapbook Bloodstone Cowboy in her citation, saying Jackson "plucks at a tangled lineage" and "brashly personifies virginity and moonshine."

years.cap: Kara Jackson, newly named National Youth Poet Laureate, Chicago, 2019
years.src: Wikipedia: Kara Jackson · The Line of Best Fit: Kara Jackson, love is as love does
years.h: Oak Park's Kara Jackson is named National Youth Poet Laureate
years.p: She was the third to hold the title, chosen after submitting an essay on poetry and democracy. Haymarket Books published her chapbook Bloodstone Cowboy the same year.
years.xp:
Smith's citation for the Literary Award praised Bloodstone Cowboy in her words: Jackson "plucks at a tangled lineage" and "brashly personifies virginity and moonshine."

Her poems had run in Poetry, Rookie and Nimrod by then. Her mother works for a labour union, and Jackson has said she grew up on protest songs.

eras.title: A guitar, a bedroom, three friends
eras.text: The poet picked up a guitar and a banjo. A small EP, a lockdown bedroom and three Chicago musicians turned into an album.

years.h: A Song for Every Chamber of the Heart, a poet's first songs
years.p: The EP is Jackson's first music: folk songs from someone better known, at that point, for her chapbook.

years.src: Wikipedia: Why Does the Earth Give Us People to Love? · The Line of Best Fit: Kara Jackson is on the rise · Smith College: Music To Love
years.h: Lockdown demos in her childhood bedroom
years.p: Jackson started recording the album's songs in her parents' Oak Park house during the first COVID lockdowns.
years.xp:
Kaina Castillo, Sen Morimoto and Nnamdi Ogbonnaya, all Chicago musicians, later came back to re-record the material for the final version.

Some songs took years to finish. Jackson has said "brain" is among the oldest.

years.src: Wikipedia: Why Does the Earth Give Us People to Love?
yt: no fun live, British Library, London
years.h: Three years after the EP, "no fun/party" sets up the album
years.p: It's her first new music since 2019. Jackson co-wrote the single with her three producers.

eras.title: The question mark
eras.text: September Recordings put out the debut in April. By December it was on year-end lists at Pitchfork, Rolling Stone and The Guardian.

years.src: BroadwayWorld: Kara Jackson Releases New Songs Dickhead Blues/Brain
years.p: Jackson released the pair three months before the album, with a lyric video for "dickhead blues".

years.src: Stereogum: Kara Jackson Announces Debut Album
years.h: Stereogum gets the first look at the album, with "pawnshop"
years.p: The site ran the record's title and release date alongside the song. Nnamdi, Kaina and Sen Morimoto produced it with her.

years.src: Album of the Year: Why Does the Earth Give Us People to Love? · Wikipedia: Why Does the Earth Give Us People to Love? · The Line of Best Fit: Kara Jackson is on the rise
years.h: Debut album Why Does the Earth Give Us People to Love?
years.p: Pitchfork gave it 8.2, named it Best New Music and ranked it No. 19 of 2023. Thirteen songs, 52 minutes, and a question for a title with no answer attached.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Mary Retta called it a "brutally honest debut" that bends folk to Jackson's will, and wrote that many songs are "harsh and disorienting, probing and uncomfortable." On Metacritic it holds a 90 from four reviews.

Jackson has said the title's question is not one the album tries to answer. Every song is co-written by the four producers except "pawnshop," which Jackson wrote with Castillo and Morimoto.
play: Why Does the Earth Give Us People to Love?

years.h: She graduates from Smith, then opens for Corinne Bailey Rae
years.p: Jackson finished an English degree in 2023 and supported Bailey Rae's Black Rainbows tour.

years.big: "Folk music is the music of the regular person."
q: Folk music is the music of the regular person. That's who I want to represent.
years.src: The Line of Best Fit: Kara Jackson, love is as love does · Wikipedia: Kara Jackson
years.h: The Line of Best Fit names it album of the year
years.p: Jackson in the interview that went with the honor. Pitchfork, Rolling Stone and The Guardian also put the record on their year-end lists.
years.xp: In the same interview she said the reception had been odd: "The weirdest part about putting my album out is people's random opinions about it."

eras.title: Chicago comes to see her
eras.text: Jackson took the album to Europe's festivals, came home to play Chicago, then started turning up on other people's records.

years.src: Vocalo: For Kara Jackson, Pitchfork Fest is a family affair
years.h: Pitchfork Music Festival puts her on the Green Stage at home
years.p: Jackson played Union Park on July 20 at 2:30 p.m. She said her parents would be there, and that Nnamdi, Kaina and Sen Morimoto had all played the festival before her.
years.xp:
She had recently played Glastonbury, Roskilde and Brosella. Jackson told Vocalo that "Pitchfork is such a familial festival for me, in general."

Her description of the sound: "While the foundation feels like folk, and I just write songs, mostly, with me and my guitar, there's so many other influences that show themselves."

yt: Orange County with Gorillaz, The Graham Norton Show
years.p: The track is on the band's ninth album, The Mountain. In May she appeared on the lead single for the Is God Is film companion album.
